articles.title: Calgary water use stays under limit for eighth straight day as crews prepare round-the-clock connection work
articles.dek: Daily use was 475 million litres on Wednesday, and crews at 33 Avenue and 89 Street N.W. move to 24-hour shifts on Saturday.
body: Calgary and the communities that share its water supply kept daily use below the 500-million-litre target for an eighth day in a row on Wednesday, as work to connect the new Bearspaw South Feeder Main moved into its second week [1][2].

The City said use reached 473 million litres on Tuesday and 475 million litres on Wednesday [1][2]. Airdrie, Chestermere, Strathmore and Tsuut'ina Nation are also covered by the restrictions and remain in what the City calls the green zone [1]. On the previous weekend, use was 482 million litres on Friday, 483 million on Saturday and 487 million on Sunday, according to figures reported at the time [3].

The City says keeping use under the target helps keep enough water on hand to fight fires, holds water pressure steady to lower the risk of a city-wide boil water advisory, and protects the system from failures that could cut off homes and businesses [1]. Stage 4 outdoor restrictions remain in effect, with no outdoor water use allowed and fines for violations starting at $3,000 [2]. A river water pick-up station is open daily from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. at the Ogden Boat Launch [2].

The new pipe will be tied in at three locations. Near the Shaganappi Pump Station, excavation is substantially complete and the tie-in pipe is exposed [1]. At 33 Avenue and 89 Street N.W., excavation is done and crews are preparing to install a new valve; starting Saturday, Nov. 14, they expect to work 24 hours a day, seven days a week for about two weeks until the connection is finished [1]. On 83 Street N.W., excavation is complete and pipe installation has started [1]. Crews are also repairing a smaller section of pipe between the Shaganappi and Memorial pump stations, with excavation underway or complete along Parkdale Boulevard N.W. [1]

Drivers should expect changes. As of Thursday, the 83 Street N.W. detour moved from 34 Avenue N.W. to 33 Avenue N.W., with single-lane alternating traffic and pedestrian detours, and drivers can no longer turn west onto 33 Avenue N.W. from 83 Street N.W. [1]

The City describes about three weeks of work remaining [1]. Michael Thompson, the City's chief operating officer for water, said earlier this week that the original pipe will be turned back on so restrictions can be lifted while the new one is commissioned, with a move to the new pipe in mid-December [3]. The City's restrictions page cautions that the old pipe remains in use and a break is still possible [2].

The restrictions come during an unusually warm, dry stretch. Thursday's forecast high for Calgary was 14 degrees above the seasonal average, with highs across southern Alberta in the high teens to low 20s [4].
key_facts: Wednesday's use: 475 million litres, under the 500-million target
Eighth straight day in the green zone
24/7 work at 33 Ave. and 89 St. N.W. from Nov. 14 for about two weeks
83 St. N.W. detour shifted to 33 Ave. N.W.

articles.title: Police seek witnesses after youth fight with weapons and a related hit-and-run in Rundle
articles.dek: Investigators say a pedestrian was struck on purpose minutes after two groups of youth fought near a playground on Rundlehorn Drive N.E.
body: Calgary police are asking for the public's help with two related incidents in the northeast community of Rundle last month: a fight between two groups of youth and a hit-and-run in which a pedestrian was struck [1].

Police say that on Monday, Oct. 19, at about 6:48 p.m., officers were called to reports of two groups of youth fighting near a playground in the 4100 block of Rundlehorn Drive N.E. [1] Officers obtained witness video showing the groups fighting with various weapons, and police believe bear spray, machetes and possibly a firearm were used [1].

About nine minutes later, at roughly 6:57 p.m., police were called to a hit-and-run involving a pedestrian in the 3800 block of Rundlehorn Drive N.E. [1] Police believe a white Mercedes SUV struck the pedestrian and that the people inside it then ran away [1]. The pedestrian was taken to hospital with injuries described as neither life-threatening nor life-altering [1].

Dashcam video from a nearby vehicle showed the pedestrian was hit intentionally, and investigators believe the fight and the collision are connected, police said [1]. No arrests or charges were announced in the release, and police did not give the ages of anyone involved [1].

Police are asking anyone who saw either incident, was in the area, or has dashcam or security camera footage of Rundlehorn Drive N.E. between about 6:30 and 7 p.m. on Oct. 19 to come forward [1]. Tips can be made by calling 403-266-1234 and quoting case number CA26481738/5395 [1].
key_facts: Fight near a playground, 4100 block Rundlehorn Dr. N.E., Oct. 19 at about 6:48 p.m.
Police believe bear spray, machetes and possibly a firearm were used
Pedestrian struck on purpose by a white Mercedes SUV minutes later

articles.title: Man in critical condition after assault near 12 Avenue and 14 Street S.W.
articles.dek: Police found the man unconscious on Sunday afternoon and say no suspects are in custody.
body: Calgary police are looking for witnesses after a man was found unconscious following an assault just west of downtown on Sunday afternoon [1].

Officers were called at about 1:23 p.m. on Sunday, Nov. 8, to the area of 12 Avenue S.W. near 14 Street S.W. for reports of an assault, police said in a release on Wednesday [1]. They found a man unconscious and he was taken to hospital with serious injuries [1]. As of Wednesday, he remained in hospital in critical condition [1].
No suspects are in custody, and police have not released a description of anyone involved or said what led to the assault [1]. The man has not been identified [1].

CTV News reported on Wednesday that police were seeking witnesses to a weekend assault in the Beltline that left one person seriously injured [2]. The police release does not use the name of the neighbourhood, so it is not confirmed that the two reports describe the same incident, although the timing and details are similar [1][2].
Police are asking anyone who was in the area at the time, or who has information, to call 403-266-1234 and quote file number CA26516076/#4657 [1].

12 Avenue S.W. near 14 Street S.W.
Man remains in critical condition

articles.title: Fire in recycling equipment forces evacuation of southeast warehouse; no injuries
articles.dek: Crews contained a fire inside a hopper at a 24 Street S.E. recycling facility, and an investigator ruled it unintentional.
body: Calgary firefighters put out a fire inside recycling equipment at a southeast warehouse on Thursday morning, and no one was hurt [1].

Crews were called at about 7:25 a.m. to a recycling facility along 24 Street S.E. for a structure fire, the Calgary Fire Department said [1]. When they arrived, light smoke was coming from inside the warehouse, and all staff had already evacuated to their muster point [1].

The fire was inside a hopper, a large container used to feed material into processing equipment, and it did not spread beyond it [1]. Firefighters and staff worked to get into the hopper to make sure the fire was completely out [1].

The warehouse sits on the west side of the landfill where a large fire broke out in September, the department said [1]. A fire investigator attended, classified Thursday's fire as unintentional and found it was not related to the earlier landfill fire [1].
key_facts: Called about 7:25 a.m. Thursday, Nov. 12
Fire contained to a hopper; staff evacuated
No injuries
Ruled unintentional and unrelated to September's landfill fire

articles.title: Flames fall 3-1 to Rangers at the Saddledome as Zibanejad scores twice
articles.dek: Calgary closed a three-game homestand at 1-1-1 and drops to 8-10-1 on the season.
body: The Calgary Flames lost 3-1 to the New York Rangers on Wednesday night at the Scotiabank Saddledome, with Mika Zibanejad scoring both of New York's first two goals [1].

Zibanejad opened the scoring 59 seconds into the second period on a shot that banked in off Calgary goaltender Devin Cooley, then added a power-play goal later in the period from a cross-ice pass by Pavel Dorofeyev [1]. Adam Klapka cut the lead in half with a power-play goal at 7:41 of the third period, assisted by Ryan Strome and Yegor Sharangovich [1]. Tye Kartye sealed the game with an empty-net goal at 19:53 [1].
Rangers goaltender Joonas Korpisalo made 29 saves, and Cooley stopped 21 shots for Calgary [1]. Alexis Lafreniere had two assists for New York [1].

The loss leaves the Flames at 8-10-1, and they finished their three-game homestand at 1-1-1 [1]. The Rangers improved to 11-8-1 [1]. Ryan Huska coaches Calgary, and this is the Flames' final season playing at the Saddledome [1].
key_facts: Final: Rangers 3, Flames 1
Klapka scored Calgary's only goal, on the power play
Flames are 8-10-1
Final season at the Saddledome
